`src/extract.js` is done and `pnpm test` passes: 18 tests pass, including the fixture test (all 77 audited values reproduced, every produced value anchored) and both contract tests. The live test was skipped because the Bright Data credentials aren't set, so it hasn't run yet.

**How it works**
- **Finding listings:** it splits `page.html` on each `goods-container` div and ends each listing at its `item-stock` div. Anything without a `goods-title` link is dropped, so other page sections don't produce rows.
- **name:** the text of the `a.goods-title` link, run through the template's own `htmlToText` and with whitespace collapsed, so it matches `page.text`.
- **price:** for listings on sale, the `goods-price-symbol` and `goods-price-value` spans, which gives text like `$ 2,549 .99` (as shown on the page). For sold-out listings, the `$…` amount inside the "Sold Price: …" note, such as `$1,799.99`.
- **stock:** the text of `goods-price-soldout` or `goods-price-comingsoon` (for example SOLD OUT, OUT OF STOCK, COMING SOON), or the `item-stock` div if it has text. In-stock listings show no stock label, so that field is left out for them.
- **Excerpts:** for each value it tries a few spans with context around it, such as the name plus its price or stock text. It keeps the first one that is under 300 characters, appears in `page.text` after whitespace normalization, and contains the value. If none qualifies, the value is dropped.

**One judgment call to check:** the audited values handle promo lines under the title inconsistently. For the two ASUS PROART listings, the name includes "Free Logitech G502 HERO gaming mouse, limited offer". For the Hasee laptop, it leaves out "Limited time offer, ends10/25". The HTML structure is the same in both cases. So the extractor adds a promo line to the name only when it starts with "Free " (a bundled gift). That rule matches this fixture, but it is an inference rather than something the page structure states. If the live page has other promo wording, the names it produces may not match what an auditor would choose.

- **Excerpts:** for each value it tries a few spans with context around it, such as the name plus its price or stock text. It keeps the first one that is under 300 characters, appears in `page.text` after whitespace normalization, and contains the value. If none qualifies, the value is dropped.

**One judgment call to check:** the audited values handle promo lines under the title inconsistently. For the two ASUS PROART listings, the name includes "Free Logitech G502 HERO gaming mouse, limited offer". For the Hasee laptop, it leaves out "Limited time offer, ends10/25". The HTML structure is the same in both cases. So the extractor adds a promo line to the name only when it starts with "Free " (a bundled gift). That rule matches this fixture, but it is an inference rather than something the page structure states. If the live page has other promo wording, the names it produces may not match what an auditor would choose.
